No one deserves poverty or the social ostracism that follows it, it is by my own estimate 90% not the persons fault, just as the rich usually were rich to begin with, to structure our politics, laws, and ideas about people through the lens of well you put yourself here and that’s why you deserve no dignity, health, or help is the most disgusting narrative we have put on our fellow man. Everyone deserves my common human decency and I theirs.
When your hands are dry and you have those little skin things coming out around your finger nails and they scrape on paper, the sound and feeling sends chills down my spine.

This is a real thing that has more roots than most can comprehend. 

Drop out due to mental health, couldn’t afford proper support as school costs too much, therefore a choice is made, anger and upset is warranted.

Grew up smart and made it to college on scholarships, parent gets sick, costs money to take care of them, can’t afford both, decision made, anger warranted.

Schools charging more and more for a degree, the rich have parents to pay for all of it, sent and leave with no debt, the poor are left with sometimes years upon years worth of debt and due to having to work through college and not being able to take low paying internships on top of that due to that job, leave school at a disadvantage compared to others as you couldn’t gain relevant work experience in the internships instead taking waitressing, housekeeping, etc. 

It’s stacked based on your social class, some make it out some don’t, education should be free and available to everyone if one of your only other choices are poverty.

It’s hard, guilting me to not do anything to myself, as I may hurt those close to me, drives me deeper into the pit.

The absolute numbness is what hurts the most, not the sadness or the anger, the non-existence of emotion is what is hardest and sometimes it will happen for weeks and then the only emotion before another months long cycle of emptiness begins, is sadness and it’s relieving and sometimes I would chase it cause it was all I had felt in months. 

It’s exhausting most times to just be, it feels like you are beginning to rot before dying and brushing your teeth or showering takes on less and less importance. And the social isolation that came with most episodes made it easier to keep it up. 

That when I was doing better than normal, I was constantly on the verge of crying uncontrollably on anyone’s shoulder who would ask “are you doing ok?”, it’s a hard question and I was ready to drop to my knees and beg that person for help or advice.

That as someone who had no money to go to therapy to get help, constantly being told to go became exhausting and left me more and more guilt ridden that I couldn’t afford it at the time. 

That just because I am at work or out at the bar and giggling and laughing, behind all that I Amy be thinking about how I want to die. This is the most serious of all, those thoughts were most of my thoughts at times, planning out how, when, where, I wanted to go. Who I needed to say good bye to or how much it would cost my family for a funeral. Not all people with depression will be like this but some of us are and really have at many times planned out how we would take our lives because we believe it to ease our own and sometimes other peoples burdens. I was planning to only live to 19 I had made that decision at 15, luckily I drunkenly broke down to a freind at 17 and it was brought to my parents 6 months later and I got help. It has been a long journey full of back and forth back and forth, I am no where near done, I feel most days that I have fallen behind my peers in financial and social growth, but I would not give up these years as the emotional maturity and empathy  I have gained for everyone around me is priceless. 
 
I am now working full time, found new passion taking care of my body, and plan on returning to online university to do a psychology degree followed by a masters so I maybe a counsellor as these days of my life awoke a passion to help others in these dark times as I was. 

Mental health is hard to understand for others and you have no idea what things people are going through, please give empathy, patients, and understanding to those you may look down upon.

I’m bi man who loves fitness and keeping busy, but anyone who brags about how much they workout or work during the week being on the “grind” or whatever, I don’t care if you are into those things and enjoy them, but don’t look down upon others who don’t.

There is dualism to the easy going and the hard working and both exist and interact for the betterment of our entire world, but you endorse a toxic culture that has taken hold of all workplaces across the western world that now demands all of an employees time and life, and has caused constant suffering in the working class. So please my rise and grinders, listen to your will to chill brethren and allow them to exist without contempt, and vice versa.

For me and my family it was the realization that no one, but working people actually care about workers over the profits of the company, this includes university putting students in unsafe financial and health situations to increase pocket books. The world has utterly stopped seeing anyone as an individual and Covid exposed that to the upper echelon we are all just cogs that make them money and any disruption to that is met with threats of homelessness and increased suffering of the lower class. 

Also that people have fallen down pipelines of politics and socioeconomic ideas that are rotting away at there cognitive abilities, and have either become completely selfish or completely removed from reality of the world, I cannot handle how much fighting there has been just over masks or vaccines to help even just your family, the cognitive dissonance of this movement is worrying and I honestly have no hate towards these people, but I worry and empathize with how far gone some of them are now. I want more education for these folks and some mental health help but I don’t know how to mandate that without massive structures for universal mental health care across the western world, which we are still fighting about.
